title: AWS temporary credentials: key ID, secret and session token
summary: AWS temporary credentials as returned by STS: an ASIA access key ID, a secret access key and a session token, in an environment export, and reordered with the session token first and the identifier last in a JSON object. Values are synthetic.
rationale: Temporary credentials are used as three values together; the session token must accompany the key pair. The secret access key span is the confidential component the provider documents. The session token and identifier are companion spans here: the pages read do not say whether the session token alone is confidential (paired unresolved case), so the case does not expect it to be flagged or ignored.

expectation.rationale: Flag the secret access key span. The STS Credentials type lists AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey and SessionToken as required values; the temporary-credentials page says a call must include the session token and that the secret key is used like a long-term one. The secret's confidentiality rests on the same reading as the long-term pair; the session token and ID are companion spans with no asserted outcome.

sources.supports: Credentials type: AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, SessionToken, Expiration all required
calls with temporary credentials must include the session token; env example sets all three values
